newsitem.title: UK: Major says UK budget to be "prudent and sensible".
newsitem.headline: Major says UK budget to be "prudent and sensible".

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Monday the government would announce a "prudent and sensible budget" in November designed to keep the country on the path of growth for years ahead.
In his annual speech to the the City of London's Lord Mayor's Banquet, Major said: "We now have a longer, more sustained recovery than any major European economy."

Unemployment was lower that the rest of Europe, inward investment rising and taxes were at their lowest basic rate for 50 years "and a lower target still before us," he said, adding: "We are not going to throw away those hard won advances."

Commentators said the budget warning, reinforced by backing for the recent decision of the Chancellor of the Exchequer, Kenneth Clarke, to raise interest rates, was a sign Major was not planning a "pre-election give-away" budget with big tax cuts.
Instead, Major signalled that the Conservatives, who must call an election in the next six months, will claim credit for the growing strength of the economy in their election campaign.
"Next year, our country will have the most secure economic base for generations. We can turn to the future and plan with confidence," he said. -- London newsroom +44 171 642 7947
